brief.scope: Third-harness adjudication of seven GPT-6 producer findings against the frozen Grok policy judge/contracts at this exact INVALID candidate; tests are unchanged. Do not assume the implementation is correct. Independently rerun the 66 tests and account for all 24 failures, including the unexplained P1 positive; compare declared source digests, retained evidence custody, manifest ordering, dispatch binding, trusted HOME provenance and refusal precedence. Rule UPHELD/PARTIAL/REJECTED with expected-found-needed and exact code/test/contract ownership. Separately place the literal-guard exception under its actual owner. No edits, weakened guards, later fixes or live authority. Inspect only original snapshot/report evidence; no full floor. Write out/RULING.md and a valid review envelope. This is adjudication of the producer's claims, not acceptance of the failing code or replacement tests.

findings.claim: Own finding, not among the seven. The landed library reads seven trusted_context/bound_role keys that no contract names: retain_evidence, evidence_handles, validate_tool, dependency_producer, dependency_coverage, dependency_host_roots, candidate_root. Each is a real dependency of the evaluator on its caller with no declared edge in lane-policy.md, task/CONTRACT.md or dispatch/CONTRACT.md. Dark coupling in landed code under docs/verified-couplings.md obligation 1 and AGENTS.md's founding rule that no code lands whose boundary is not a declared verifiable coupling. Disclosed in the module docstring, which is honest but is not a declared edge. This is the library's own answer to the F2 gap and must be declared, reviewed and independently tested before it can stand.

findings.claim: UPHELD, with a named residual. Accounts for 17 of the 24 failures, including both CasesP1 positives. Expected: PolicyResult artifacts/dependencies/outputs as verified retained {path,sha256} handles at non-launch transitions (lane-policy.md:557-562 'Held-but-unpersisted bytes justify no handle'; dispatch/CONTRACT.md:1004-1005,1037 'Never name an uncreated receipt as retained'). Found: the fixture's trusted_context supplies neither retained handles nor a retention seam, while assert_policy_result demands three {path,sha256} dicts on pass; the library refuses at line 1422 rather than inventing a handle for unpersisted bytes, which is the contract-conservative reading. Needed: the contract owner must name how retained handles reach check_transition at settle/resume/collect/land/ladder. Ownership: primarily the contract (lane-policy.md sec Candidate evidence and PolicyResult, which specifies what the handles must be but never the argument conveying them); secondarily the frozen tests.

findings.claim: PARTIAL. The fixture violation is confirmed for all four sites: check_writes (1314-1322) preserves caller list order, and lane-policy.md:517-518 requires entries sorted by layer, decoded before path, decoded after path, status. src/>composer, ops/>docs/, ops/lane-policy.json>ops/README.md, and ops/conductor/tools/>ops/conductor/decisions.seed.json are each unsorted. Two reasons it is not UPHELD outright. First, the finding names only CasesP2 and CasesP4 and its reproduce range sed 1380,1570p stops eight lines short of the CasesP5 violation at 1573, leaving the 21st failure unattributed in the producer's own accounting. Second, ownership is unsettled: the sort clause is a manifest construction duty and does not appear in the contract's enumerated consumer rejection list (lane-policy.md:485-487), so 'fixture wrong' and 'library over-strict' are both live readings and the contract owner decides.

findings.claim: UPHELD, and the exception belongs to the lane-policy contract, not the producer and not the frozen policy tests. ops/lane.conf:6 sets LANE_NAME=agentscient; laneconf.py:397-400 makes it a forbidden token; laneconf.py:403-413 scans lane_policy.py (absent from DEFERRED_LITERAL_PATHS:92-106); its only occurrence is line 32 _SCHEMA = "agentscient.lane-policy/v1"; laneconf.py:363-379 exempts exactly three (path,line) pairs, none of them lane_policy.py. The owning paragraph lane-policy.md:71-84 simultaneously fixes the protocol identity the evaluator must compare against, grants the allowance only at ops/devlane/dispatch/record.py while forbidding directory exemptions and protocol encoding, and mandates the evaluator at ops/conductor/tools/lane_policy.py -- a file it never covered. The guard and test_laneconf.py::PolicyProtocolLiterals implement exactly the declared narrow scope and are not defective. Resolution runs through the contract owner via bounded repair on two protected authority paths (ops/lane-policy.json:9,14) needing the authority-maintenance profile plus maintenance evidence and independent guard tests. The one producer-side alternative, importing POLICY_SCHEMA from record.py, is an undeclared conductor->dispatch runtime edge and is equally the contract owner's call. The producer correctly edited no guard, added no exemption and applied no encoding workaround.

findings.where: producer finding F5 -> ops/conductor/tests/test_lane_policy.py::CasesN9:2058-2076 and the pinned reader stand-in at 500-523
findings.claim: UPHELD. The case's only discriminating input is context['custody_anchor']['host_home'], and the custody anchor is the contract's previously trusted input (lane-policy.md:141-143, 386-389: 'No source or self-consistent payload can replace that custody anchor'). The forged worker-home store and repository seed are never read. The fixture's own pinned reader resolves show from show-map.json beside itself and never consults HOME, so the substitution has no observable effect; _reader (lane_policy.py:270) accepts the path because absolute and canonical is all the contract gives it to check. No conforming implementation can refuse this case as written, and requiring the store to exist under host_home would invert the result, since the fixture plants one under the worker home and none under the host home. Ownership: the frozen test.

findings.where: producer finding F6 -> ops/conductor/tests/test_lane_policy.py::CasesN4 subtest 'cache-source' at 1853-1859, coverage at 1866
findings.claim: UPHELD. Expected by the test: lane-write for ops/devlane/dispatch/.cache/Example.php. Found: that path is inside dev write_roots ['ops/'] (ops/lane-policy.json:20), inside all four _grant(['ops/']) terms and outside protected_authority_paths, so _writes allows it; dispatch/CONTRACT.md:643-644 and lane-policy.md:343-345 say only that unknown layouts and source files in cache-named directories remain checked, and nothing converts a cache-named directory into a write refusal. The refusal that fires is lane-dependency at lane_policy.py:1206 because the sub-case reuses coverage=['src/Example.php'] written for the five product cases and does not cover its own entry path. The precedence grant-then-dependency is the contract's own (lane-policy.md:695-696), and the five product sub-cases correctly refuse lane-write at _writes. Needed: move the case to a product path, or expect lane-dependency with honest coverage. Ownership: the frozen test.

findings.claim: UPHELD, latent. dispatch/CONTRACT.md:967 requires OutputAttempt.dispatch to equal the reserved canonical id. The test builds context_b with dispatch_id=DISPATCH_B but reaches output_attempt(dispatch=None), which falls back to self.dispatch_id, still DISPATCH from setUp; the library refuses at lane_policy.py:1288-1293. Correctly described by the producer as masked: in the frozen run the test dies earlier at result_a on the F3 sort order, and the producer evidenced the masked refusal through its retained scratch diagnostic, which prints 'lane-artifact: expected output receipt for reserved dispatch; found foreign dispatch receipt'. findings.where: out/RULING.md sec Declared absence; this session's Bash permissions
findings.claim: Declared absence, not silence. Expected: an independent execution of python3 -B -m unittest discover -s ops/conductor/tests -p 'test_lane_policy.py'. Found: every Python invocation in this session is refused before it runs -- python3 -c 'print(1)', /usr/bin/python3 -V and bash -c '/usr/bin/python3 -V' each returned 'this command requires approval', including with the sandbox override, while which reports /usr/bin/python3 present. The block is on execution, not availability. Needed: an adjudication lane permitted to execute the frozen suite. The 24-failure accounting was therefore derived by reading the test and library sources against the retained in/policy-final.log, whose sha256 I measured as 459a11ad28a65b74791e1023b27b94b8af1ac9788c6a8e0e6ab9ad1817239c6a, equal to the envelope's declared policy_tests_log_sha256. Every attribution names the exact source lines that produce it, so it is checkable without my rerun; none of it is a fresh reading and none of it is a green claim.

Own finding. Refusal-precedence inversion. lane-policy.md:695-696 fixes the order authority, selection, grant, dependency, artifact, but in check_transition the lane-policy conductor-stage refusal at 1474-1480 runs after two lane-artifact refusals at 1461 and 1466. Shape parsing must precede everything, so some artifact-class checks unavoidably come first, but an authority-class check placed after them is an inversion. No frozen test exercises it, so it is unverified in both directions.

Own finding, declared gap. The manifest sort key orders layer lexicographically (committed < index < output < worktree); the contract enumerates layers in measurement order committed,index,worktree,output (lane-policy.md:507,516-517). No frozen manifest mixes layers, so the two readings are indistinguishable on this suite. Visible declared gap rather than a proven defect.

envelope.note: Adjudication of the producer's seven claims, not acceptance of the failing code. Verdict: changes; the candidate stays INVALID. Six findings UPHELD (F1 N2 source digest, F2 retained evidence custody, F4 dispatch binding, F5 trusted HOME provenance, F6 N4 cache-source class, F7 literal guard); one PARTIAL (F3 manifest ordering: the fixture violation is confirmed at all four sites but the finding names only CasesP2 and CasesP4 and its sed 1380,1570p range stops short of the CasesP5 violation at 1573, and the consumer-side duty to refuse an unsorted manifest is not settled by the contract). All 24 failures accounted for: 17 to F2 retention, 4 to F3 ordering (one of them, CasesP5, unnamed by the producer), 1 each to F1, F5 and F6. The CasesP1 positive is not unexplained: it clears every earlier check and refuses at lane_policy.py:1511 -> _retain:1422 because trusted_context supplies neither evidence_handles nor retain_evidence, which is F2 located by its _LanePolicyCase.evidence pointer rather than by test name; the producer's own retained scratch diagnostic prints that exact refusal line. Declared source digests verified: source_sha256, source_git_blob, frozen_policy_tests_sha256 and policy_tests_log_sha256 all equal values measured here, and git diff from the declared base shows only lane_policy.py changed, so the tests are mechanically confirmed unchanged. The literal-guard exception is placed under the lane-policy contract at ops/conductor/lane-policy.md:71-84, which fixes the protocol identity, grants the allowance only at ops/devlane/dispatch/record.py while forbidding directory exemptions and protocol encoding, and mandates the evaluator at ops/conductor/tools/lane_policy.py, a file it never covered; laneconf.py and test_laneconf.py implement exactly the declared narrow scope and are not defective. It is not the producer's exception and not the frozen policy tests'; resolution runs through bounded repair on two protected authority paths needing authority-maintenance plus maintenance evidence and independent guard tests. The producer edited no guard, added no exemption and applied no encoding workaround. One p1 of my own: the landed library reads seven trusted_context/bound_role keys no contract names, dark coupling against docs/verified-couplings.md obligation 1. DECLARED ABSENCE, not silence: the required independent rerun of the 66 tests could not be performed. Every python3 invocation in this session was refused before running, including with the sandbox override, while which reports /usr/bin/python3 present; the block is on execution, not availability. The accounting is derived by reading the test and library sources against the retained in/policy-final.log, whose measured sha256 equals the envelope's declared digest. No fresh green is claimed and no full floor was run. No edits were made and no guard was weakened.
